definitions.gloss: to replant; to transplant; to repot
definitions.explanation: To move a plant from one location or container to another. Common in gardening contexts.

examples.japanese: {花|はな}を{大|おお}きい{鉢|はち}に{植|う}え{替|か}えた。
examples.english: I replanted the flower in a bigger pot.

examples.japanese: {春|はる}になったら{苗|なえ}を{庭|にわ}に{植|う}え{替|か}える{予定|よてい}だ。
examples.english: I plan to transplant the seedlings to the garden in spring.

examples.japanese: {根|ね}が{詰|つ}まってきたので、そろそろ{植|う}え{替|か}えた{方|ほう}がいい。
examples.english: The roots are getting crowded, so you should repot it soon.

notes:
USAGE:
Primarily a gardening term. The noun form {植|う}え{替|か}え refers to the act of replanting/repotting. Spring is the most common time for {植|う}え{替|か}え in Japan.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {鉢|はち}に{植|う}え{替|か}える (to repot)
- {庭|にわ}に{植|う}え{替|か}える (to transplant into the garden)
- {植|う}え{替|か}えの{時期|じき} (repotting season)
- {苗|なえ}を{植|う}え{替|か}える (to transplant seedlings)
